en.heading: 24 October: the Charter that brought the United Nations into existence
en.origin: The United Nations officially came into existence on 24 October 1945 when its founding Charter entered into force after the necessary ratifications, including those of all five permanent Security Council members. Two years later, on 31 October 1947, the General Assembly established a dedicated United Nations Day through resolution 168 (II). Celebrations began in 1948, and in 1971 the Assembly recommended that Member States observe it as a public holiday. The date therefore commemorates the birth of the Organization, not the later day on which the commemorative resolution was adopted.
en.promoter: The General Assembly instituted the annual commemoration in 1947. The Charter had been negotiated and ratified by founding Member States in 1945; neither historical action identifies one individual founder of the observance.
en.purpose: Explain the goals of the UN Charter and how international cooperation on peace, development, rights and humanitarian work depends on the commitment of its Member States.
facts: The Charter entered into force on 24 October 1945.
General Assembly resolution 168 (II) declared United Nations Day in October 1947.
Resolution 2782 (XXVI) of 1971 recommended public-holiday observance by Member States.

it.heading: 24 ottobre: la Carta che ha fatto nascere le Nazioni Unite
it.origin: L'ONU nacque ufficialmente il 24 ottobre 1945, quando entrò in vigore la Carta delle Nazioni Unite dopo le ratifiche richieste, comprese quelle dei cinque membri permanenti del Consiglio di sicurezza. Il 31 ottobre 1947 l'Assemblea generale istituì una giornata dedicata con la risoluzione 168 (II). Le celebrazioni iniziarono nel 1948 e nel 1971 l'Assemblea raccomandò agli Stati di considerarla festività pubblica. La data ricorda quindi la nascita dell'Organizzazione, non il giorno della successiva risoluzione commemorativa.
it.promoter: La giornata fu proclamata dall'Assemblea generale nel 1947; la Carta era stata precedentemente negoziata e ratificata dagli Stati fondatori nel 1945.
it.purpose: Spiegare gli obiettivi della Carta ONU e come la cooperazione tra Stati sostenga pace, sviluppo, diritti umani e interventi umanitari.
facts: La Carta delle Nazioni Unite entrò in vigore il 24 ottobre 1945.
L'Assemblea generale dichiarò la giornata con la risoluzione 168 (II) del 1947.
Nel 1971 la risoluzione 2782 (XXVI) suggerì agli Stati di celebrarla come festività.

en.heading: 24 October: making development issues visible through information
en.origin: In 1972, the General Assembly instituted World Development Information Day through resolution 3038 (XXVII), deliberately assigning it the same date as United Nations Day. The choice also recalls 24 October 1970, when the Assembly adopted the International Development Strategy for the Second United Nations Development Decade. The original purpose was to raise public understanding of development challenges and mobilize cooperation, especially among young people. Information access, today's digital divide and reliable public communication remain central to the day; the original act does not document a distinct first annual event.
en.promoter: The UN General Assembly established the observance in 1972, referencing both its own 1970 development strategy and the existing United Nations Day.
en.purpose: Encourage informed public participation in development policy, international cooperation and more equitable access to reliable information and communications technology.
facts: Resolution 3038 (XXVII) established World Development Information Day in 1972.
24 October also marks the 1970 adoption of the Second Development Decade strategy.
The original UN purpose included involving young people through greater public awareness.

L'obiettivo originario era sensibilizzare l'opinione pubblica sulle disuguaglianze e mobilitare la cooperazione, coinvolgendo specialmente i giovani. en.heading: 27 October: saving films, recordings and voices from disappearing
en.origin: In 2005 UNESCO's thirty-third General Conference proclaimed 27 October World Day for Audiovisual Heritage, linking it to the anniversary of UNESCO's 1980 Recommendation for the Safeguarding and Preservation of Moving Images. Film reels, sound recordings, television archives and other formats can deteriorate chemically or become unreadable when playback equipment disappears. The day therefore concerns more than cinema nostalgia: audiovisual collections preserve languages, testimonies and everyday experiences that may not survive in written records. The formal 2005 designation is distinct from the 1980 standard, and the first annual worldwide commemoration is not asserted without evidence.
en.promoter: UNESCO's General Conference proclaimed the observance in 2005, commemorating its earlier 1980 recommendation; audiovisual archivists and preservation institutions are key partners rather than single documented founders.
en.purpose: Promote ethical digitization, cataloguing, conservation and public access to endangered film and sound heritage while respecting creators' rights.
facts: 27 October refers to the UNESCO Recommendation on moving images adopted in 1980.
The formal World Day was proclaimed at UNESCO's 33rd General Conference in 2005.

Pellicole, registrazioni sonore e archivi televisivi possono deteriorarsi oppure diventare illeggibili quando scompaiono i dispositivi necessari. La giornata non riguarda soltanto il cinema: questi documenti conservano lingue, testimonianze e gesti quotidiani spesso assenti nei testi scritti. La proclamazione del 2005 è distinta dalla raccomandazione del 1980; l'anno della prima celebrazione mondiale non viene dato per certo.
it.promoter: La Conferenza generale UNESCO istituì la ricorrenza nel 2005 richiamando una propria raccomandazione del 1980; archivi e cineteche partecipano alla conservazione senza essere fondatori unici dimostrati.
it.purpose: Promuovere digitalizzazione responsabile, catalogazione, conservazione e accessibilità ai documenti audiovisivi tutelando i diritti degli autori.

en.heading: 29 October: the United Arab Emirates' coding-day proposal becomes a UNESCO event

en.heading: 29 October: care work becomes an issue of rights and public policy
en.origin: The UN General Assembly adopted A/RES/77/317 on 24 July 2023 and established 29 October as the International Day of Care and Support, with an annual date later that same year. Care is both paid labour in health, social and domestic services and unpaid work performed within families. The resolution calls on governments to recognise, reduce and redistribute unpaid care and to strengthen decent conditions for paid carers. It was not the beginning of care work or the international movement for carers' rights. The official founding text establishes the date without demonstrating an exact anniversary for 29 October.
en.promoter: The General Assembly made the formal 2023 proclamation; UN Women, the ILO and human-rights agencies support its implementation but are not automatically proven to have authored the original proposal.
en.purpose: Recognize care as vital social infrastructure, improve conditions for paid carers and distribute unpaid responsibilities more fairly across societies.
facts: The founding General Assembly resolution was adopted on 24 July 2023.

it.heading: 29 ottobre: il lavoro di cura entra nelle politiche pubbliche

La cura comprende sia il lavoro retribuito in sanità, servizi sociali e assistenza domestica sia quello non pagato nelle famiglie. La risoluzione chiede di riconoscere, ridurre e redistribuire la cura non retribuita e migliorare le condizioni delle lavoratrici e dei lavoratori del settore. en.heading: 31 October: World Cities Day begins with Shanghai
en.origin: The General Assembly established World Cities Day in December 2013 through A/RES/68/239, designating 31 October for annual celebration. en.heading: 2 November: the killings of two journalists in Mali become a global warning
en.origin: In December 2013 the General Assembly adopted A/RES/68/163, establishing 2 November as the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists. The date specifically commemorates the murder of two French radio journalists in Mali on 2 November 2013. A statement by the President of the General Assembly documents the inaugural UN observance in 2014. The day demands investigation and accountability for assaults on journalists, because intimidation and unpunished killings also deprive the wider public of reliable information. The victims are the event commemorated, not the political authors of the resolution.
en.promoter: The UN General Assembly instituted the international date in 2013; UNESCO and journalists' safety organisations support related monitoring and campaigns.
en.purpose: Demand independent investigations and protection for media workers, challenging impunity and safeguarding access to public-interest reporting.

en.heading: 3 November: biosphere reserves link nature and communities
en.origin: At its forty-first General Conference in 2021, UNESCO proclaimed 3 November the International Day for Biosphere Reserves, with the first annual UNESCO observance following in 2022. Biosphere reserves belong to UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere Programme, initiated in 1971, and are recognised because they combine biodiversity conservation, research and the sustainable use of landscapes by local communities. They are not identical to strict nature reserves excluding all human activity. UNESCO's new date raises awareness of this living laboratory model; the reviewed proclamation does not establish a specific earlier anniversary as the reason for 3 November.
en.promoter: UNESCO's Member States at the General Conference adopted the day in 2021, building on the older Man and the Biosphere Programme and its international network.
en.purpose: Encourage stewardship of biodiversity and practical cooperation between researchers, Indigenous and local communities and sustainable livelihoods.

en.heading: 5 November: the rice-sheaf fire that warned a coastal village
en.origin: The United Nations General Assembly designated 5 November as World Tsunami Awareness Day in December 2015 through A/RES/70/203. Japan proposed the initiative, drawing on its long experience of devastating waves and early-warning systems. A footnote to the founding resolution explains the particular date through the 1854 'Inamura-no-hi' account: a villager reportedly set fire to rice sheaves to warn neighbours of an approaching tsunami and later worked to rebuild the community. The first annual UN observance followed in 2016. The lesson is that warnings save lives when people recognise danger and know where to evacuate.
en.promoter: Japan advanced the international day through the UN, which adopted its resolution in 2015; the 1854 village story explains the date rather than proving a modern individual founder.
en.purpose: Promote hazard education, accessible early-warning systems, coastal evacuation plans and community drills before disaster strikes.

en.heading: 6 November: recognising the environment as a victim of warfare
en.origin: On 5 November 2001 the General Assembly adopted A/RES/56/4, proclaiming 6 November the International Day for Preventing the Exploitation of the Environment in War and Armed Conflict. Wars can poison soil, pollute water, destroy crops and leave damaged ecosystems that continue to threaten civilians after fighting ends. The observance draws attention to natural-resource pressures as possible contributors to insecurity and to environmental restoration as part of durable peace. A 2016 UN Environment Assembly resolution later reinforced this approach. The founding act does not prove a specific historical anniversary for 6 November.
en.promoter: The General Assembly established the day in 2001; UNEP and environmental peacebuilding researchers contribute knowledge, not an identified sole originator.
en.purpose: Encourage protection of water, soil, forests and wildlife during conflicts and include environmental recovery in reconstruction and peacebuilding.

UNEP has documented strong links between some internal conflicts and natural-resource pressures.

Le ostilità possono avvelenare suoli, contaminare acqua, bruciare raccolti e lasciare ecosistemi danneggiati anche dopo la fine dei combattimenti. La ricorrenza richiama il ruolo delle risorse naturali nelle tensioni e il recupero ambientale nella costruzione di una pace duratura. Una risoluzione dell'Assemblea ONU per l'ambiente del 2016 rafforzò poi questo orientamento. Non è dimostrato un anniversario particolare per il 6 novembre.

en.heading: 10 November: science becomes a public conversation about peace
en.origin: UNESCO proclaimed World Science Day for Peace and Development at its thirty-first General Conference in 2001, with the first annual events taking place in 2002. It arose from discussions about connecting scientists with wider society, notably following the World Conference on Science in Budapest in 1999. The observance does not celebrate one discovery or a single scientist; it highlights scientific evidence as a resource for peaceful cooperation and sustainable development. UNESCO's official page establishes the 10 November date without demonstrating a particular historic anniversary for its choice.
en.promoter: UNESCO Member States adopted the 2001 proclamation, advancing the wider scientific-community discussions after the World Conference on Science.
en.purpose: Strengthen public engagement with science, collaboration among researchers and responsible use of knowledge for peaceful and sustainable societies.
facts: UNESCO proclaimed the international day in 2001 and first celebrated it in 2002.

it.heading: 10 novembre: la scienza dialoga con la società per la pace
it.origin: L'UNESCO proclamò la Giornata mondiale della scienza per la pace e lo sviluppo durante la trentunesima Conferenza generale del 2001; le prime iniziative annuali seguirono nel 2002. en.heading: 14 November: Banting's birthday and the history of diabetes awareness

en.heading: 15 November: fighting organised crime across borders
en.origin: In March 2024 the UN General Assembly adopted A/RES/78/267 and designated 15 November as the International Day for the Prevention of and Fight against All Forms of Transnational Organized Crime. The observance recalls the legal framework created when the Assembly adopted the Convention against Transnational Organized Crime in November 2000. Organised networks traffic people, drugs, wildlife and illicit goods, launder money and increasingly exploit online systems. The date invites cooperation between investigators and public institutions without conflating enforcement with a substitute for victim protection and the rule of law.

en.heading: 15 November: a prematurity campaign changes date as it joins WHO

en.heading: 16 November: Mediterranean food heritage becomes a global observance
en.origin: In 2025 the United Nations General Assembly adopted A/RES/80/174 and declared 16 November the International Day of the Mediterranean Diet. The observance highlights food culture rooted in olive oil, vegetables, cereals, legumes, seasonal practices and social meals around the Mediterranean. en.heading: 16 November: UNESCO's Declaration of Tolerance becomes an annual date

en.heading: 17 November: five years from a WHO strategy to a formally designated day
en.origin: On 17 November 2020 WHO launched its Global Strategy to accelerate the elimination of cervical cancer as a public-health problem. en.heading: 18 November: protecting children and supporting survivors of abuse
en.origin: In November 2022 the UN General Assembly adopted A/RES/77/8, designating 18 November as a world day for preventing and healing from child sexual exploitation, abuse and violence. The observance takes a survivor-centred approach: preventing harm, providing confidential support and helping children recover are all essential, while the responsibility for abuse never lies with the victim. en.heading: 19 November: a civil-society sanitation campaign becomes a UN day

en.heading: 20 November: industrial development on Africa's own terms

L'Italia sostenne poi un progetto per istituire il 21 novembre come Giornata mondiale della televisione, approvato dall'Assemblea generale con A/RES/51/205 il 17 dicembre 1996. La data ricorda l'apertura del forum, mentre la prima annualità dopo l'atto fu nel 1997. en.heading: 24 November: families of conjoined twins receive global recognition
en.origin: The UN General Assembly proclaimed 24 November World Conjoined Twins Day through A/RES/78/313 on 1 July 2024, explicitly setting observance from 2024. The original draft A/78/L.72 was introduced by Bahrain, Saudi Arabia and ten other countries from several regions. The condition arises during early embryonic development and may involve complex medical, family and accessibility needs. The new day emphasises respectful language, social inclusion and appropriate health support rather than treating affected children as curiosities. The original resolution does not explain a specific historic anniversary behind 24 November.

en.heading: 25 November: the Mirabal sisters and a movement that predates the UN day
en.origin: Women's rights activists have commemorated 25 November since 1981, remembering three Mirabal sisters, political opponents of the Dominican dictatorship who were murdered in 1960. The UN adopted the Declaration on the Elimination of Violence against Women in 1993 and, on 7 February 2000, formally designated 25 November through A/RES/54/134. This history shows that a date shaped by regional feminist activism later gained global institutional recognition. The day addresses violence against women and girls in both public and private life; the United Nations did not originate the 1981 movement.

en.heading: 26 November: transport is about access, not only vehicles
en.origin: The UN General Assembly adopted A/RES/77/286 in 2023, proclaiming 26 November World Sustainable Transport Day. The resolution highlights safe, affordable and accessible ways for people and goods to move, from buses and railways to ports, roads and walking routes. Sustainable transport depends on planning and inclusion as well as cleaner vehicles: it can reduce pollution while opening access to schools, jobs and services. The 2023 designation follows decades of UN transport and development policy rather than creating mobility cooperation for the first time. The original act does not establish a specific anniversary explaining 26 November.

La proclamazione segue decenni di politiche internazionali sulla mobilità, senza un anniversario specifico dimostrato per la data.

en.heading: 26 November: the olive tree as a symbol of peace and resilience
en.origin: At the fortieth General Conference in 2019 UNESCO proclaimed 26 November World Olive Tree Day. Olive trees have shaped landscapes, agricultural economies and cultural traditions around the Mediterranean for thousands of years, and the olive branch has become a widely recognised symbol of peace. The new international day invites countries to consider biodiversity, heritage and sustainable management of ancient trees and cultivated groves. It is an act of UNESCO's Member States rather than the creation of olive farming itself. The official UNESCO page does not establish a unique original individual founder or a historical anniversary explaining 26 November.

en.heading: 27 November: a new UN commitment to end child and forced marriage
en.origin: On 4 September 2026 the UN General Assembly adopted A/RES/80/309, declaring 27 November the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage. en.heading: 29 November: the 1947 partition resolution behind a solidarity day
en.origin: In December 1977 the UN General Assembly called for an annual International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People through resolution 32/40 B. The 29 November date marks the adoption, on that day in 1947, of Assembly resolution 181 (II), which envisaged partition of Palestine into an Arab and a Jewish state with a special international regime for Jerusalem. The observance provides a forum for discussion of Palestinian rights and the United Nations' responsibilities. A historic UN decision and the later commemorative act are separate; the date does not imply that the 1947 proposal was implemented as written.
en.promoter: The General Assembly created the annual commemoration in 1977; the Committee on the Exercise of the Inalienable Rights of the Palestinian People coordinates related activities.
en.purpose: Keep attention on the rights and aspirations of Palestinians through peaceful, fact-based dialogue and UN diplomatic processes.

en.heading: 30 November: chemical-weapons remembrance moves from April
en.origin: The Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons established a memorial day for chemical-warfare victims in 2005, originally on 29 April, the anniversary of the 1997 entry into force of the Chemical Weapons Convention. At its twentieth session in 2015, the OPCW Conference of States Parties decided through C-20/DEC.10 to observe it on 30 November or, where appropriate, the first day of the regular Conference session. The present date therefore reflects a subsequent scheduling decision, not the original anniversary. The day honours victims while reaffirming the commitment to eliminating chemical weapons.

en.heading: 1 December: the first global health day devoted to AIDS
en.origin: World AIDS Day was first marked on 1 December 1988 as an international public-health campaign led through the World Health Organization, before the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS was created. en.heading: 2 December: a 1949 convention anchors today's anti-slavery observance
en.origin: The International Day for the Abolition of Slavery is observed on 2 December, marking the General Assembly's adoption on 2 December 1949 of the Convention for the Suppression of the Traffic in Persons and of the Exploitation of the Prostitution of Others, resolution 317 (IV). en.heading: 2 December: UNESCO asks everyone to think about possible futures
en.origin: On 23 November 2021 UNESCO's forty-first General Conference proclaimed 2 December World Futures Day, with its first international celebration held at UNESCO headquarters in Paris in 2022. The initiative was supported by the United Arab Emirates and builds on UNESCO's work in futures literacy, the capacity to imagine different futures and use those possibilities to make better decisions now. This is not a prediction contest; it brings together researchers, young people, policymakers and communities to reflect on uncertainty and long-term resilience. en.heading: 4 December: recognising banks' role in financing sustainable development
en.origin: On 19 December 2019 the United Nations General Assembly adopted A/RES/74/245, proclaiming 4 December International Day of Banks. The first annual date after the resolution was in December 2020. The original act recognises both multilateral development banks that finance long-term projects and domestic banking systems that support households and businesses. en.heading: 4 December: a contested policy issue receives a UN observance
en.origin: On 16 June 2025 the General Assembly adopted A/RES/79/293, establishing 4 December as the International Day against Unilateral Coercive Measures. The first UN observance followed later in December 2025. These measures can include restrictions on trade or finance imposed outside collective UN Security Council arrangements. it.heading: 4 dicembre: un tema controverso entra nel calendario ONU

en.heading: 5 December: the soil-science community and Thailand shape a world day
en.origin: The International Union of Soil Sciences proposed a dedicated World Soil Day in 2002. en.heading: 9 December: a genocide treaty anniversary becomes a day of dignity
en.origin: On 29 September 2015 the UN General Assembly adopted A/RES/69/323, proclaiming 9 December the International Day of Commemoration and Dignity of the Victims of the Crime of Genocide and of its Prevention. en.heading: 11 December: the International Year of Mountains leaves an annual legacy
en.origin: The United Nations named 2002 the International Year of Mountains, drawing attention to fragile highland ecosystems and people whose livelihoods depend on them. en.heading: 12 December: Turkmenistan's neutrality becomes an annual UN theme
en.origin: On 2 February 2017 the UN General Assembly adopted A/RES/71/275 without a vote, proclaiming 12 December International Day of Neutrality. en.heading: 12 December: a health-coverage promise becomes an annual call to action
en.origin: On 12 December 2012 the General Assembly adopted A/RES/67/81, urging countries to accelerate universal health coverage: quality health services without financial hardship. en.heading: 14 December: the 1960 decolonization declaration gains a new anniversary
en.origin: In 2025 the United Nations General Assembly adopted A/RES/80/106, creating 14 December as the International Day against Colonialism in All Its Forms and Manifestations. en.heading: 15 December: the Orkhon inscriptions and a language-family day
en.origin: At its forty-third General Conference in Samarkand on 3 November 2025, UNESCO adopted a resolution declaring 15 December World Turkic Language Family Day. Türkiye and fellow Turkic-speaking countries drafted the proposal. The date specifically recalls 15 December 1893, when Danish scholar Vilhelm Thomsen announced the decipherment of the Orkhon inscriptions as written in Turkic, a milestone in the study of early written Turkic languages. The day celebrates linguistic diversity and the shared cultural heritage of many communities, without implying that all Turkic languages are identical. A first independently verified official celebration is not asserted here.

en.heading: 18 December: Arabic's recognition at the UN explains the language day
en.origin: UNESCO has celebrated World Arabic Language Day on 18 December since 2012. The date recalls the General Assembly's decision of 18 December 1973 to adopt Arabic as the sixth official language of the United Nations. Arabic's diverse written, spoken and literary forms have long shaped scholarship, poetry, science and cultural exchange across regions. UNESCO's celebration should not be confused with the creation of the language or the UN's 1973 institutional decision itself: it is a later initiative to acknowledge linguistic diversity. The UNESCO programme promotes dialogue and access to knowledge through Arabic.

en.origin: On 31 August 2026 the UN General Assembly adopted A/RES/80/301, designating 19 December as the International Day of Recognition for Women Searchers of Missing Persons. en.heading: 20 December: solidarity becomes a stated international value
en.origin: In December 2005 the UN General Assembly adopted A/RES/60/209, proclaiming 20 December International Human Solidarity Day. The first annual date after the proclamation was in 2006. The observance encourages practical international cooperation rather than treating solidarity as a purely sentimental slogan. Poverty reduction, shared responsibility and international commitments are central themes; the founding act does not establish a particular anniversary explaining 20 December.

en.origin: In December 2024 the General Assembly adopted A/RES/79/137, proclaiming 21 December World Meditation Day. en.heading: 27 December: the COVID-19 era brings epidemic preparedness into the calendar
en.origin: In December 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic, the General Assembly adopted A/RES/75/27 and designated 27 December the International Day of Epidemic Preparedness.
